title: The business cycle
log: 2026-11-12T12:44:15Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: No bank point teaches the business cycle as booms and slowdowns read through indicators at Year 9-10 depth; the closest, the AS output gap and trade cycle card, centres on output gaps at a much more advanced level, and the other cards cover indicators or GDP without the cycle itself.

draft.title: The business cycle
card: The economy does not grow at an even pace. It moves through ups and downs over time. This pattern is called the business cycle.
a period of strong growth. Real GDP rises quickly, jobs are easy to find and unemployment is low. Price rises often speed up.
a period of weak or negative growth. Real GDP rises slowly or falls, firms hire fewer workers and unemployment tends to rise. Price rises often ease.
Indicators such as GDP growth, unemployment and inflation show which phase the economy is in. After a slowdown, growth picks up again and a new upswing begins.
draft.remember: The economy swings between booms and slowdowns, and indicators show which phase it is in.

a.q: Which set of changes in indicators best fits a boom?
opts: Fast GDP growth and falling unemployment
Fast GDP growth and rising unemployment
a.why: In a boom, output grows quickly and firms hire more workers, so unemployment falls. Fast growth with rising unemployment does not fit, because strong growth usually creates jobs.
a.clue: In a boom, are firms hiring more or fewer workers?

b.q: In one year, a country's real GDP growth falls from 4% to 0.5%, and its unemployment rate rises from 4% to 6%. What does this suggest?
opts: The economy is moving into a slowdown
The economy is moving into a boom
The economy has stopped following a cycle
The economy is growing faster than before
b.why: Weaker growth and higher unemployment are signs of a slowdown. A boom would show faster growth and falling unemployment, the reverse of these figures.
b.clue: Look at which way growth and unemployment moved.

wants.brief: A wavy line of real GDP over time rising and falling around a rising trend. Label the high points 'Boom' and the low points 'Slowdown'. Label the axes 'Time' and 'Real GDP'.
wants.why: Seeing the ups and downs shows that growth is uneven.

a.best: Fast GDP growth and falling unemployment

b.best: The economy is moving into a slowdown
